sections.label: Prioritising applicants with Singapore ties
sections.summary: One proposed change is to prioritise applicants with stronger ties to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: First, one proposed change is to prioritise applicants with stronger ties to Singapore.

sections.label: Disqualifying applicants with serious offences
sections.summary: The change makes disqualifying applicants who committed serious offences the default, rather than reviewing all applications case by case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Second, the change of default to disqualifying applicants who have committed serious offences, rather than allowing all applications and then reviewing on a case-by-case basis.

sections.label: Bill allows single parents to adopt
sections.summary: The Bill allows for single parents to adopt, a provision the speaker says is left implicit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As much as I support this Bill for what it makes explicit, I would also like to point out an important provision of this current Bill and what it leaves implicit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This Bill allows for single parents to adopt.

sections.label: Applicants must notify material changes
sections.summary: The proposed change puts the onus on applicants to notify authorities of any material change in their circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Second, in ensuring that assessments are current and also recognising that the entire process can take some time – potentially up to three years – the current proposed change is to put the onus on the applicants to notify authorities of any material change in their circumstances.

sections.label: Adoption reserved for stable family units
sections.summary: The speaker emphasises that adoption should be reserved for stable family units, ideally with a married husband and wife.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: They each have different personalities, but, when they are put together, they make quite a team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I would also like to emphasise that it is in the best interests of children that adoption should be reserved for stable family units, ideally with a married husband and wife.

sections.label: Support for no commercial surrogacy policy
sections.summary: The speaker supports Singapore's continued policy of generally not allowing commercial surrogacy, to protect children and birth mothers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Alongside this, in order to protect children and also birth mothers, I also support Singapore's continued policy of, generally, not allowing commercial surrogacy.

sections.label: Adoptive parent and birth mother lists
sections.summary: A suggestion for MSF to invite prospective adoptive parents and pregnant women wanting adoption to put their names on lists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: One humble suggestion is for MSF to invite prospective adoptive parents to put their names down on a list, and also to have a list of pregnant ladies who want to give life to their babies, but cannot take care of them and would like to put them up for adoption.

sections.label: Follow-up support for adoptive parents
sections.summary: A call on MSF to provide follow-up support, engagement and bonding activities for parents of adoptive children who desire support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Like all families, there are ups and downs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, I call on MSF to provide follow-up support, engagement and bonding activities for parents of adoptive children who desire support.

sections.label: Dispensing consent and adopter eligibility
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Court dispense with birth parents' consent if they are unfit or unwilling, and bars persons convicted of serious crimes from adopting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill states that the Court may dispense with a child's birth parents' consent to the adoption if the birth parents are unfit or unwilling to care for the child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill also prevents persons convicted of serious crimes, such as sexual violence and drug-related offences, from adopting and I would like to make two points on this matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, I am happy to see that the Bill recognises the reformation process and the Court may consider exceptional cases for overcomers to be eligible for adoption.

sections.label: Non-traditional families and updating legislation
sections.summary: The speaker acknowledges other non-traditional family structures may meet an adopted child's needs, and notes the Act was last substantially amended in 1985.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While I do not disagree with the Government's position against deliberate single parenthood through surrogacy, adoption or same-sex parents, I am pragmatic in acknowledging the possibility that other non-traditional family structures may be able to meet the needs of an adopted child just as efficiently.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The last substantial amendment to the Act was in 1985, almost 40 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The recommended increase from 12 sections to 75 sections in the proposed amendments, is a testament to the need to update this legislation.

sections.label: Adoption process steps and Yen's wait
sections.summary: The adoption process involves many steps, and Yen, an adoptive mother, waited for a Dependant's Pass before spending time with the child.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The process of adoption, currently, involves many steps – from pre-adoption briefing, to home assessment study, identifying an agent, identifying a child for adoption, applying for a Dependant's Pass for a foreign child, getting the approval of the Family Court, sending the Adoption Order to ICA for a birth certificate, applying for Singapore Citizenship and, in the case of China, several post-adoption reporting requirements. "Yen", a happy adoptive mother who adopted a baby from an ASEAN country, had to wait for a Dependant's Pass to be approved before she could spend time with the child, even after passing a very stringent Home Report assessment.

sections.label: Publishing agency details and evaluating agencies
sections.summary: Clause 10 provides for publishing authorised adoption agencies' UEN and business address, and the speaker asks how MSF will evaluate appropriate agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Whilst the new clause 10 of the Bill provides for the Unique Entity Number (UEN), address of the place of business of every authorised adoption agency to be published, one wonders if that is sufficient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Lastly, on the voice of the adoption agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is obvious from the feedback from adoptive parents I spoke to that not all adoption agencies are equally experienced, ethical and effective.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How will MSF evaluate and identify appropriate agencies?

sections.label: Fee guidelines for adoption agencies
sections.summary: Asks whether fee guidelines like MOH's could set an acceptable range of service fees so good adoption agencies remain in business.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Can there be fee guidelines such as that issued by the MOH for clinics, so that there is an acceptable range of service fees?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This will ensure that adoption agencies with good records get to remain in the business and build on their strength to support more families effectively.

sections.label: Additional information under clause 14(3)
sections.summary: Asks the Minister to clarify what additional information is required under clause 14(3)A and B.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify what additional information is required as prescribed under clause 14(3)A and B?

sections.label: Estimated ASA fees and capping
sections.summary: Asks whether the Minister can indicate estimated ASA fees adoption agencies will charge and whether the Government would cap them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Bearing in mind that each HSR already costs $2,000 and the HSR process is currently undertaken by commercial agencies, is the Minister able to indicate, for now, the estimated fees which the Government expects the adoption agencies to charge for ASA and would this be capped by the Government?

sections.label: Adoption cost increase concern
sections.summary: Urges the Government to ensure the Bill will not increase the cost and expenses of adoption, especially for overseas children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Certainly, for the many adoption cases involving children from overseas each year, the cost is considerable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to take steps to ensure that this Bill will not lead to an increase in the cost and expenses of adoption.

sections.label: Safeguards for court adoption decisions
sections.summary: Seeks the Minister's assurance that sufficient safeguards remain so adoptions under clause 37 conditions are allowed only in the most appropriate cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Even after the passing of this Bill, it will not and should not be an easy decision for the Court to make based on any set of general conditions, such as those in clause 37, for example, the time consideration which should be given to the parents in each type of situation listed in the clause, or for each particular case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I seek the Minister's assurance that there will still be sufficient safeguards to ensure that any adoption in these circumstances be allowed in perhaps only the most appropriate of cases.

sections.label: Oath for adopted children born overseas
sections.summary: Asks whether the law could dispense with the oath for children not born in Singapore adopted by Singaporeans, and notes the Bill codifies MSF briefing practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider amending the law to dispense with the need for such adopted children not born in Singapore to take this oath, especially for children who were formally adopted by Singaporean parents under Singapore law within a short time after birth, for example, say, not more than one to two years after birth, and whose adoptive parents are also Singaporeans at the time of issuance of the children's Singapore citizenship certificate and birth certificate?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Many of the adopted children would have severed their ties with their former countries, as well as their birth parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This Bill codifies the existing practice required by MSF for all would-be adoptive parents to first attend certain briefings, including a briefing on disclosure of adoptive status in clause 13.

sections.label: Disclosure briefings in adoption Bill
sections.summary: The Bill includes disclosure briefings, which the speaker says helps enshrine the importance of disclosure, though parental disclosure is not mandated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While still not mandating disclosure by parents to their adopted children of the status of their adoption, the inclusion in the Bill of the disclosure briefings is still, in my view, extremely significant, as it would help to enshrine the importance of disclosure.

sections.label: Adoption toll and disclosure briefing
sections.summary: The episode affected his parents' marriage, and the speaker was briefed early in adoption on the importance of disclosure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Sadly, the episode also took a toll on his parents' marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I was glad that in the early stages of adoption, I was briefed and made to understand the importance of disclosure.

sections.label: Bill revises adoption process protections
sections.summary: The Bill revises adoption, refreshing protections for biological parents and amending rules on suitability of providers and adoptive parents for the child's welfare.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Bill that is being debated here takes important steps to revise the process of adoption, refreshing some protections for biological parents while simultaneously introducing a number of amendments to ensure the suitability of adoption providers and adoptive parents for the sake of the welfare of the most important individual in the adoption process – the child.

sections.label: Pre-adoption procedures and suitability assessments
sections.summary: The Bill codifies pre-adoption procedures, requiring prospective parents to undergo suitability assessments, a home study report, and pre-adoption and disclosure briefings.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One important objective of this Bill is to codify a number of sound and sensible procedures related to pre-adoption procedures, including requiring prospective parents to undergo suitability assessments – what, in practice, results in a home study report as well as attending pre-adoption and disclosure of adoption briefings.

sections.label: Adoption steps and two-year limit
sections.summary: Steps including at least two Court hearings, interviews and MSF background investigation may be prolonged but should not exceed two years under clause 31(1).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The various steps involving at least two Court hearings prior to the issuance of the order of adoption, interviews in the office as well as at home after the arrival of the child and background investigation by MSF may be prolonged but, as clause 31(1) of the Bill indicates, should not exceed two years.

sections.label: Timeline changed to 21 months
sections.summary: In 2019, the timeline was altered to allow 21 months after the Dependant's Pass was first issued.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2019, this timeline was altered to allow 21 months after the Dependant's Pass was first issued.

sections.label: Migrant domestic worker levy concession
sections.summary: The existing migrant domestic worker levy concession rate is not available for families whose children are on a Dependant's Pass, and the $240 difference adds up for families facing startup expenses.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Similarly, the existing migrant domestic worker levy concession rate is not available for families whose children are on a Dependant's Pass.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The $240 difference can quickly add up, especially for families that are already facing a surge of startup expenses that go towards new furniture, equipment, diapers and milk powder.

sections.label: Adoptive mothers leave entitlement
sections.summary: This leave is an entitlement only for adoptive mothers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For starters, this leave is an entitlement only for adoptive mothers.

sections.label: Child citizenship eligibility criteria
sections.summary: The eligibility criteria require the child to become a citizen within six months of the adoption.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the eligibility criteria require the child to become a citizen within six months of the adoption.

sections.label: Minister cancelling adoption agency authorisation
sections.summary: Clause 10(5) allows the Minister to cancel the authorisation of an authorised adoption agency before the expiry of the authorisation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The closest we see to such language in the Bill is that clause 10(5) allows the Minister to cancel the authorisation of an authorised adoption agency before the expiry of the authorisation.

sections.label: MOM oversight and adoption benefits
sections.summary: MOM oversees migrant domestic worker agencies closely and can revoke licences for repeated or especially egregious violations, while the Bill's rules rationalise the adoption process in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: MOM oversees migrant domestic worker (MDW) agencies closely and agencies that engage in repeated or especially egregious violations can expect to have their licences revoked.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It relieves biological parents who have neither the wherewithal nor inclination to raise a child on their own; it offers adoptive parents an opportunity to fulfil their dreams of raising a child; it provides an opportunity for a child to have a better start in life.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is also a win for our country – as Singaporeans struggle with delayed marriages and low fertility rates, adoption offers a means for our families to start or expand families that would otherwise not result.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The rules introduced in this Bill go a long way towards rationalising the adoption process in Singapore.

sections.label: Adoption in child's best interests
sections.summary: MSF is repealing and re-enacting the Adoption of Children Act 2022 to better safeguard adopted children's welfare, and for joint applicants both individuals should be habitually resident in Singapore, with either or both being citizens or both being PRs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As it takes great love, sacrifice and long-term commitment to adopt a child, the process must be considered in the best interests of the child identified for adoption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am heartened to know that MSF is repealing and re-enacting the Adoption of Children Act 2022 to better safeguard the welfare of adopted children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For joint applicants, I note that both the individuals should be habitually resident in Singapore, and either or both of the individuals are citizens of Singapore, or both individuals are PRs.

sections.label: Adopter suitability and HSR fee
sections.summary: The speaker raises suitability assessment for prospective adopters and notes the current HSR fee is $2,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My third point relates to the suitability assessment for all prospective adopters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also note that the current HSR fee is set at $2,000.

sections.label: Support services for adopted children
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MSF consider support services for adopted children up to age 21, citing mental health and behavioural development risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Given the mental health and behavioural development risk associated with adopted children, I would like to suggest that MSF consider providing support services to adopted children up to the age of 21 when they can lead an independent life.

sections.label: Protecting adopted children's safety and welfare
sections.summary: The speaker says adoption requires adoptive parents' love and dedication, and new Bill provisions protect children's safety and welfare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The adoption of a child is a very important decision that requires unwavering love and selfless dedication of the adoptive parents to fulfil the promise of a home to the adopted child.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe that the safety and well-being of the adopted children are the key factors in determining whether they can find a happy home, conducive for their development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The new provisions added to the Bill are in line with this guiding principle of protecting the safety and welfare of children.

sections.label: Support for the Adoption Bill
sections.summary: The speaker says adoption with legislative framework and social support serves children's welfare, and supports the Bill despite considerations raised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Adoption is a beautiful thing and, with the necessary legislative framework and social support in place, I believe that it will serve the interest and welfare of children identified for adoption and create a journey filled with hope ahead for the children and the parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my considerations raised, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Adoption option amid child abuse rise
sections.summary: The speaker says adoption may be the best option for a normal childhood, and the Bill is timely given rising child abuse cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For these kids, adoption may be the best option for them to lead a normal and healthy childhood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill is timely, given the sharp rise in child abuse cases within the past two years.

sections.label: Adoption by convicted persons
sections.summary: The speaker asks what exceptional circumstances may permit adoption by a person convicted of serious crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, what are some exceptional circumstances that may permit adoption by a person who has been convicted of serious crimes?

sections.label: Time-bar duration decision
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry decides on the time-bar duration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How does the Ministry decide on the time-bar duration?

sections.label: Adoptions of children in state care
sections.summary: A news report says fewer than 10 applications concern children in state care, out of about 400 yearly adoption applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: According to a news report, there are fewer than 10 applications for children in state care, out of about 400 adoption applications filed in Singapore yearly.

sections.label: Government help over two years
sections.summary: Over the last two years the Government has done much to help Singaporeans save jobs and support workers and companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Over the last two years, the Government has done much to help fellow Singaporeans to save jobs and to provide emergency support for workers and their companies.

sections.label: Helping those in need
sections.summary: In helping those in need, such as children in challenging family circumstances, strengths and abilities are leveraged to create a stronger social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In helping those in need, such as children who struggle through challenging family circumstances, we leverage our various strengths and abilities to create a stronger social compact.

sections.label: Adoptions and adoptees' matches
sections.summary: The passage urges helping make every adoptee-adopter match a success, expresses admiration for Singaporeans who adopted, and cites an average of 400 adoptions yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Let us help in every way we can, to make every match between adoptees and adopters a success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Lastly, I would like to express my admiration and appreciation for the Singaporeans who have adopted children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to data from MSF, there is an average of 400 adoptions a year in Singapore.

sections.label: Adoption without birth parents' consent
sections.summary: The Bill clarifies thresholds, circumstances and more grounds for Courts to allow adoption without the birth parents' consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: However, I have a few clarifications and suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: However, couples who wish to adopt such children face roadblocks when the child's birth parents do not consent to the adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: To address this issue, the Bill makes clearer the proposed thresholds and circumstances and specifies more grounds, under which the Courts will allow the adoption to proceed without the birth parents' consent.

sections.label: Foster care numbers stable
sections.summary: MSF data shows children and young persons in foster care stayed stable at about 540 over the past three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to MSF data, the number of children and young persons in foster care has remained stable at about 540, in the past three years.

sections.label: Adoption leave and childcare leave
sections.summary: Adoptive mothers of children below 12 months get 12 weeks paid adoption leave; for children aged 12 months to seven years, parents get six days GPCL.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Presently, adoptive mothers of children below the age of 12 months are entitled to 12 weeks of paid adoption leave, which they can use to bond with, and care for their adopted newborns and infants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For adopted children aged between 12 months and seven years old, adoptive parents can only tap on six days of Government-paid childcare leave (GPCL).

sections.label: Primary and secondary school fees
sections.summary: Primary school fees are over $800 per month, while secondary school fees range between $1,000 and $2,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For Primary schools, the fees are over $800 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For Secondary schools, they range between $1,000 and $2,500.

sections.label: Children adopted each year
sections.summary: On average, 400 children are adopted each year and half are born in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: On average, 400 children are adopted each year and half of them are born in Singapore.

sections.label: Regulating the adoption sector
sections.summary: The passage proposes regulating adoption sector parties, implementing safeguards against applicants convicted of serious crimes, and prioritising applicants with a strong nexus to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: First, regulate the key parties of the adoption sector, to ensure that they are well-run and to deter them for commodifying the adoption process; second, implement safeguards against the applicants convicted of serious crimes – children who are put up for adoption deserves to belong to supportive and healthy families; third, prioritising applicants with a strong nexus to Singapore.

sections.label: Adoption versus fostering decisions
sections.summary: The passage asks MSF how the Government decides whether children are put up for adoption versus fostering and whether the new ACA will change such decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Lastly, I would like to ask MSF how the Government decides whether children are put up for adoption versus fostering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Will the new ACA lead to any changes when the Government makes such decisions?

sections.label: Adoption Suitability Assessment requirement
sections.summary: Under section 11, only individuals with a valid and favourable Adoption Suitability Assessment may make an adoption application.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under section 11, an adoption application may only be made by an individual holding a valid and favourable Adoption Suitability Assessment (ASA).

sections.label: Dispensation of consent grounds
sections.summary: The Bill allows dispensation of consent of relevant persons on grounds of ill-treating or failing to provide suitable care for the child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My second point is on the dispensation of consent of relevant persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill allows for the dispensation of consent of relevant persons on the grounds of having ill-treated or failing to provide any suitable care for the child.

sections.label: Commercial adoption agencies unregulated
sections.summary: Commercial adoption agencies are not directly regulated today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Commercial adoption agencies are not directly regulated today.

sections.label: MSF age gap guidance
sections.summary: MSF had said the couple should not be more than 50 years older than the child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MSF had said that the couple should not be more than 50 years older than the child.

sections.label: Adoption Bill addresses challenges
sections.summary: The speaker is encouraged that Singapore's tabled Adoption of Children Bill addresses legal and administrative challenges in adoption, enabling safe, ethical placement.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: For this reason, I am encouraged and grateful to note how Singapore's tabled Adoption of Children Bill addresses many of the legal and administrative challenges faced in the adoption process; paving the way for children to be placed in Singapore homes in a manner that is safe, ethical and brings fulfilment to both children and their adoptive parents.

sections.label: Children in state care
sections.summary: In Singapore, over 1,000 children are in state care in residential and foster homes, though not all require adoption.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: In Singapore alone, there are over 1,000 children in state care staying in residential and foster homes, even if not all require adoption.

sections.label: Adoption applications and state care
sections.summary: Adoption support was over 80% in 2013, applications fluctuated around 380 from 2012 to 2021, and fewer than 10 yearly were for children under state care.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: While over 80% of Singaporeans surveyed in 2013 shared that they are supportive of adoption, the number of adoption applications in Singapore has fluctuated around 380 from 2012 to 2021.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: And of these adoption applications, fewer than 10 per year are for children under state care.

sections.label: Adopted child and government support
sections.summary: An adopted child said adoptive parents gave life, and the Government wants more families adopting children under state care.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: An adopted child once shared: "My birth mother brought me into this world, but it was my adoptive parents who gave me life."  As a Government, I believe we can do more to raise awareness, advocate for and support families in adoption.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: As a nation, I look forward to the day where we will have more families wanting to adopt, waiting to adopt children, than children waiting on families, especially for our Singaporean children under state care.

sections.label: Social workers checking adopted children
sections.summary: The question asks whether social workers would be assigned to check on these children for the first two to three years after adoption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would social workers be assigned to check on these children for the first two to three years after they are adopted?

sections.label: Disclosure Briefing for prospective adopters
sections.summary: Disclosure is not mandatory, but the Disclosure Briefing encourages prospective adopters to disclose adoptive status and equips them with skills and knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While disclosure is not mandatory, the Disclosure Briefing aims to encourage prospective adopters to disclose to the child the truth about his or her adoptive status and equip the couples with the necessary skills and knowledge to make the disclosure.

sections.label: Register with birth parents' agreement
sections.summary: The question asks whether a register with some basic information could be established with the agreement of the birth parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Is it possible to establish a register with some basic information, of course, with the agreement of the birth parents?

sections.label: Authorities setting up register
sections.summary: The question asks whether the authorities will set up a register with some basic information.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Will the authorities set up a register with some basic information?

sections.label: Serious offences for adoption screening
sections.summary: The guiding principle for prescribing serious offences is the offence's bearing on applicants' character, fitness and ability to care for a child, including sexual abuse, violence and Children and Young Persons Act offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: To address Ms Ng Ling Ling's query on how we will determine the types of serious offences to be prescribed, our guiding principle will be the bearing that the offence has on applicants' character and fitness and their ability to safely care for a child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Such offences would include sexual abuse and violence offences and offences under the Children and Young Persons Act.

sections.label: Child welfare and no time-bar
sections.summary: The overriding consideration is whether the child's welfare is protected, and there is no fixed time-bar before an ex-offender can become eligible to adopt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The overriding consideration is, again, whether the child's welfare is protected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: I would also like to inform Mr Yip Hon Weng that there is no fixed time-bar before an ex-offender can become eligible to adopt.

sections.label: Mandatory ASA for all applicants
sections.summary: ASA will be mandatory for all applicants, even if they are related to the child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The key difference is that ASA will be mandatory for all applicants, even if they are related to the child.

sections.label: Interviews and periodic declarations
sections.summary: Household members and close family members and friends who may meet the child are interviewed, and periodic affirmations and declarations by prospective adopters would be useful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In fact, we also interview their household members, as well as those close family members and friends who may meet the child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We agree with Mr Seah Kian Peng that periodic affirmations and declarations by prospective adopters on their circumstances would be useful.

sections.label: MSF requires adopter declarations
sections.summary: MSF will require prospective adopters to provide declarations along the adoption process, consistent with placing the onus on them to notify material changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Consistent with placing the onus on prospective adopters to notify MSF and authorised adoption agencies of material changes in their circumstances, MSF will require them to provide such declarations along the adoption process.

sections.label: Simplified ASA for prolonged care
sections.summary: Where applicants have cared for the child for a prolonged period and preliminary investigations show no concerns, authorised adoption agencies may issue a simplified ASA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In cases where the applicants have been caring for the child for a prolonged period and do not present any concerns based on preliminary investigations, authorised adoption agencies may issue a simplified ASA.

sections.label: Adopter information and assessments
sections.summary: The Bill empowers GIA and authorised adoption agencies to direct prospective adopters to provide information or undergo assessments, including psychological or psychiatric ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Under the Bill, GIA and the authorised adoption agencies will be empowered to direct prospective adopters to provide any pertinent information or undergo assessments, including psychological or psychiatric assessments, to better assess their physical and mental fitness.

sections.label: Disclosure guidelines for children
sections.summary: Broad guidelines say disclosure should be a process, sensitive to the child's emotions and needs, and assure the child of being loved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Broad guidelines for disclosure would include broaching disclosure as a process, rather than as a one-off event, being sensitive to the child's emotions and needs in understanding his or her birth history and assuring the child that he or she is loved.

sections.label: Studying greater disclosure steps
sections.summary: The speaker says steps towards greater disclosure, such as an adoption register, will be further studied.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: As I mentioned in my opening speech, we will further study steps we could take towards greater disclosure, such as the setting up of an adoption register.

sections.label: Adoptive family treated as family
sections.summary: After an adoption order follows extensive investigations, MSF's general position is to treat the adoptive family as any other family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: An adoption order is made after extensive and in-depth investigations are conducted to ensure that the child is placed with suitable adoptive parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Hence, after an adoption order is made, MSF's general position is to treat the adoptive family as any other family.

sections.label: Court-ordered support services
sections.summary: Rigorous assessments and guidance should suffice, but under the Bill the Court can order parties to undergo support services like mediation or counselling after proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: If we conduct the pre-adoption suitability assessments rigorously and guide adoptive parents well in their adoption journey, it should suffice to offer support services to those who may need them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: That said, under the Bill, even after proceedings have concluded, the Court can order parties to undergo support services, such as mediation or counselling.

sections.label: Grounds for dispensing consent
sections.summary: Consent may be dispensed with only when a birth parent cannot consent or unreasonably withholds it and adoption is in the child's welfare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Our intent is for a birth parent's consent to adoption to be dispensed with only when he or she is unable to provide consent or is, unreasonably, withholding such consent and adoption would be in the child's welfare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We also looked at other jurisdictions' laws on dispensation, examined the adoption applications that MSF has seen over the years and consulted professionals involved in contested adoption cases to determine the threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Hence, the grounds are based on actual cases where it has been tested and shown clearly that the child is unlikely to be reunified safely with his or her birth family and adoption would be in the child's welfare.

sections.label: Reunification timelines by child age
sections.summary: For children below three, 12 months with birth parents indicates reunification likelihood; for those above three, about 24 months is taken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Generally, for children below three years of age, working with birth parents for a period of 12 months provides MSF with a good indication of the likelihood that the child can be reunified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For children above three years of age, a longer duration of about 24 months is taken.

sections.label: Bill's first outcome
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to achieve three main outcomes, the first being to find a good home for every child identified for adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We thank the Members for raising these issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to achieve three main outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: First, to find a good home for every child identified for adoption.

sections.label: Balancing birth parents and child
sections.summary: The Bill balances the interests of birth parents and the child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Second, the Bill balances the interests of birth parents and the child.

sections.label: Deterring undesirable adoption practices
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to deter undesirable practices in the adoption sector by putting in place a strong regulatory system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Lastly, the Bill seeks to deter undesirable practices in the adoption sector by putting in place a strong regulatory system.
